summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and recurrent tracheitis was admitted for increased cough, green and blood-tinged tracheal secretions, throat pain, and dizziness. She had recently completed a course of antibiotics for a prior infection. Evaluation showed no fever, normal white blood cell count, and a chest X-ray without pneumonia. A sputum culture was contaminated and deemed invalid. Given the absence of infection signs, antibiotics were not restarted. Her symptoms were attributed to inflammation rather than active infection. She remained stable, and plans for an outpatient T-tube to tracheostomy exchange with ENT were confirmed. She was discharged home with a short-term supply of oxycodone-acetaminophen for pain, with clear instructions to avoid other acetaminophen or opioid products.
